title: Bioprintable Alginate/Gelatin Hydrogel 3D In Vitro Model Systems Induce Cell Spheroid Formation
protocol: Wash and dry 250 mL and 100 mL glass beakers, magnetic stirrers, spatulas, 10 mL cartridges, and 25 G cylindrical nozzles.
Autoclave the materials at 121 °C for 15 minutes under 1 atm pressure.
Sterilize alginate and gelatin powders, paraffin film, aluminum foil pieces of 5 cm², 1 mL syringes, and 5 mL syringes under UV light for at least 4 hours.
Immerse end caps, tip caps, and pistons in 70% ethanol for at least 4 hours.
Wash the end caps, tip caps, and pistons twice with sterilized ultra-pure water.
Weigh 3 g of alginate and 7 g of gelatin.
Dissolve 4 g of agarose with ultra-pure water.
Autoclave the dissolved agarose.
Filter a 100 mM solution of anhydrous calcium chloride in sterilized ultra-pure water through a sterile filter with a pore size of 0.22 μm prior to use.
Melt sterile agarose in a microwave to obtain a liquid solution.
Add 2 mL of melted agarose per well in a Biosafety Cabinet using a 1 mL micropipette.
Mix the agarose gently to create a uniform layer in the bottom of each well.
Cool down the wells and seal them with paraffin film.
Store the sealed wells at room temperature until use.
Mix 3 g of alginate and 7 g of gelatin powders into a 250 mL beaker within a Biosafety Cabinet.
Add a magnetic stirrer and 100 mL of DPBS to the beaker.
Seal the beaker with sterile paraffin film and aluminum foil.
Dissolve the powders under constant agitation at 600 rpm for 1 hour at 60 °C in a BSC.
Continue dissolving at room temperature for an extra 2 hours.
Heat the material at 37 °C until it undergoes a phase transition to the liquid state (45 min for 100 mL).
Transfer the solution into sterile 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes.
Seal the tubes and centrifuge them at 834 x g for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the hydrogel precursor into 10 mL syringes.
Seal the syringes with caps and paraffin film.
Store the sealed syringes at 4 °C until use.
Mix 100 mL of fetal bovine serum (FBS) with 10 mL of an antibiotic/antimycotic solution in a fresh sterile container.
Add DMEM medium to adjust the mixture up to 1,000 mL.
Seal the container and keep it at 4 °C.
Defrost 1 vial of MDA-MB-231-GFP cells from liquid nitrogen storage by gently moving it into a water bath at 37 °C.
Defrost 1 vial of IMR-90-mCherry cells from liquid nitrogen storage by gently moving it into a water bath at 37 °C.
Transfer 160 µL/well of cell solution (3 x 10^6 cells/mL) into a 6-well plate.
Add 5 mL of warmed (37 °C) basal DMEM medium to each well.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C/5% CO2 for 24 - 48 h until the cells reach 80% confluence.
Discard the medium after the cells reach confluence.
Rinse the cells twice with DPBS.
Incubate the cells with 500 µL of trypsin-EDTA solution/well at 37 °C for 6 min.
Inactivate the trypsin by adding 500 µL of FBS to each well.
Recover the cell solution and transfer it to T-75 flasks.
Incubate the cells again at 37 °C/5% CO2 until they reach 80% confluence.
Warm up the hydrogel precursor in a 37 °C water bath for 1 h.
Turn on the air compressor connected to the rheometer and let it run for 30 min.
Switch on the temperature control box for the rheometer, switch on the rheometer itself, and switch on the computer connected to the rheometer.
Open the rheometer software, click Initialize on the control panel, and let the initialization process finish.
Set the platform temperature to 37 °C on the control panel.
Click the Measuring set tab and navigate to the Start service function.
Select Adjust driver inertia in the drop-down menu and click Start adjustment in the pop-up window.
Mount a parallel measuring tool in the rheometer.
Set zero-gap on the control panel and wait for the procedure to finish.
Pay attention to the normal force during this process.
Navigate to the Start service function under Measuring set tab.
Select Adjust upper measuring system inertia from the menu.
Click Start adjustment in the pop-up window.
Allow the measuring tool to move up by clicking the triangle button on the control panel.
Conduct an amplitude sweep.
Click Start, then click Insert in the top menu.
Select Wait from the drop-down menu.
Set the waiting time to 2 h in the setup window.
Click Start again, then click Insert button.
From the drop-down menu, select Device and choose Temperature.
Set Temperature to be 25 °C without waiting until value is reached.
Click Measurement step, then click variable Oscillation strain.
Pull up the setup window, set Profile to Ramp logarithm.
Change initial strain to 0.001% and final strain to 100%.
Set frequency at 0.01 Hz.
Add Temperature variable by clicking Add button.
Set Temperature to be 25°C in the pull-up window.
Expand Calculator, set Point density to 10 points/decade.
Take the syringe out of the water bath and extrude approximately 0.5 mL of the precursor onto the rheometer platform.
Click the downwards triangle button on the control panel.
Wait for the measuring tool to move down to the trimming position.
Use a spatula to trim any excess precursors that escaped at the edge of the measuring tool and discard the superfluous material.
Pipette mineral oil onto the edge of the measuring tool and wait until the oil fully seals the boundary.
Click Continue on the control panel.
Click the Start button (green triangle).
Click the Continue button at the bottom screen.
When the testing is done, release the measuring tool.
Click the upwards triangle button on the control panel.
Remove the measuring tool and clean it with 70% ethanol.
Clean the platform with 70% ethanol.
In the current project, click the step Measurement and pull up the setup window.
Set the frequency to 100 Hz.
Keep all other parameters unchanged.
Repeat steps 2.4.5 - 2.4.10.
Click Diagram.
Observe the curve of G’, G” versus the oscillation strain.
Find the deflection points of G’ for both frequencies (0.01 Hz and 100 Hz).
Find the corresponding oscillation strains for both deflection points.
Choose the smaller oscillation strain.
Use 1/10 of this strain for all oscillation tests conducted afterward.
Click Table and copy all data from the test into a text file.
Conduct a temperature sweep.
Click My apps and select the template Temperature ramp, oscillatory shear: Gelation.
Name the project.
Click Measurement in the workflow.
Click the variable Temperature, pull up the setup window, and set the initial temperature to 37 °C and final temperature to 25 °C.
Set oscillation strain to 0.1%, oscillation frequency to 1 Hz.
Set number of data points to be 61.
Set data collection frequency to 1 point/min.
Click Calculator and set Point density to 0.2 °C/point.
Load the sample on the rheometer platform.
Perform the test by following steps 2.4.5 - 2.4.10.
Click Diagram, observe G’, G” versus temperature.
Find the crossover point of G’ and G”.
Determine the temperature at the crossover point.
Repeat step 2.4.15.
Conduct an isothermal time sweep.
Click My apps and find the template Isothermal time-temperature test.
Click the step Measurement in the workflow, then click the variable Oscillation strain.
Set the oscillation strain to 0.1%.
Set the oscillation frequency to 1 Hz.
Set the number of data points to 120.
Set the data collection frequency to 1 point/min.
Add the Temperature variable by clicking Add button.
Click variable Temperature in the middle window and set it to 25 °C.
Right click the step Device move to measuring point, then delete it.
Uncheck the box Wait until value is reached for the step Device set value.
Set value to 25 °C.
Click Picture, tittle, buttons at the bottom screen, then uncheck the box Continue.
Name the project and save it.
Load the sample onto the rheometer platform.
Start the test by following steps 2.4.5 - 2.4.10.
Observe G’, G” versus time.
Find the crossover point of G’ and G”.
Determine the time at the crossover point.
After completing the test, click Table.
Copy all data from Table.
Paste the copied data into a text file.
Measure the yield strength at various gelling times.
Click My apps and find the template Yield and flow stress, Gel-like.
Name the project.
Click Start in the workflow.
Insert a Wait step and set the waiting time to be 20 min.
Choose Temperature device and set it to 25 °C without waiting until value is reached.
Select Shear stress variable for Measurement step.
Set initial shear stress to 0 Pa and final shear stress to 10,000 Pa.
Set Point density to 0.2 point/Pa in the Calculator setup.
Set Data points tab to 1 point/second.
Set stop criterion in Event control tab: stop measurement if shear rate > 100 s-1.
Load the sample onto the rheometer platform and start the test.
Click Diagram to observe the strain-stress curve.
Find the deflection point of the strain and its corresponding stress.
Repeat steps but change waiting time to 30, 40, and 50 min for each replicate.
Arrange a path that connects the nodes.
Assign a cartridge for the inner circle, the middle sectors, and the outer sectors.
Set the layer thickness to be 150 µm.
Set the number of layers to be 4.
Let the program output a text file in G-code format recognizable by the bioprinter.
Set m = 2.
Set n = 5.
Run the script and retrieve the generated G-code file.
Copy and paste the file to the bioprinter’s dedicated G-code folder.
Turn on the bioprinter and its control software.
Initialize the printer.
Open the G-code script just created.
Set all pressures to zero in the G-code script.
Return to the control software.
Click the tab Scaffolder generator.
Click the Run button at the right bottom corner.
Observe the moving path of the printer.
Sterilize the bioprinter by spraying 70% ethanol thoroughly.
Expose the bioprinter to UV light overnight.
Take out a syringe of the hydrogel precursor (at 4 °C).
Warm the hydrogel precursor in a water bath at 37 °C for 1 h.
Take the T-flask with cells from the CO2 incubator and place it inside a BSC.
Discard the culture medium and rinse the cells with DPBS twice.
Add a warmed trypsin-EDTA solution (3.0 mL) and incubate the cells at 37 °C for 6 min.
Inactivate the trypsin with an equal volume of FBS.
Count the cells using trypan blue assay.
Take the syringe of the hydrogel precursor from the water bath, clean it, and sterilize it with 70% ethanol.
Put the syringe into the BSC.
Extrude approximately 3 mL of hydrogel precursor into a 10 mL printing cartridge.
Mix the precursor with MDA-MB-231-GFP cells at 1 x 10^6 cells/mL by slowly pipetting it, avoiding the production of bubbles.
Cover the cartridge with the sterile end and top caps and seal it with paraffin film.
Centrifuge it at 834 x g for 1 min to eliminate any gas bubbles produced.
Repeat steps for the IMR-90-mCherry cell-laden precursor and the cell-free precursor.
Sterilize all 3 cartridges with 70% ethanol.
Load the sterilized cartridges into the chambers of the bioprinter.
In the printer’s control software, set the cartridge temperature to 25 °C.
Wait 35 min to allow the precursor to reach printable conditions.
Measure the position of the nozzle tip for each of the three cartridges using the Measure short button in the printer’s control software.
Place a clear polystyrene microplate on the printing platform.
Change the pressure settings to 200 kPa for all cartridges via the G-code file.
Click the Run button in the Scaffolder generator tab to start printing one replicate.
Repeat step to print three more replicates.
Add a 100 mM CaCl2 solution to cross-link the printed models for 1 minute.
Rinse the models twice with DPBS to remove excess Ca++ ions.
Transfer the models onto an agarose-coated 6-well plate using a spatula.
Add 5 mL of DMEM media to each well containing the models.
Incubate the plates in an incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Replace the cell culture medium with fresh medium every three days.
Culture the hydrogel disks for a total of 30 days.
Use a sterile graduated 1 mL syringe.
Cut the nozzle to create a large hole in the syringe with the same diameter as the rest of the syringe tube.
Clean the syringe with 70% ethanol and leave it until dry.
Place the syringe in a sterile BSC.
Add 100 mM CaCl2 to a well-plate lid until the surface is covered.
Fill the syringe with cell-laden hydrogel.
Extrude 100 µL of hydrogel using the hanging drop method.
Leave the extruded hydrogel for 1 min.
Rinse the hydrogel with excess DPBS.
Transfer the hydrogel disks onto an agarose-coated 6-well plate.
Add 5 mL of basal DMEM to each well.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for up to 30 days.
Refresh the medium every 3 days.
Wash each disk with DPBS.
Cut the disk into four parts with a fine sterile blade.
Transfer the parts to a 96-well plate.
Add 100 μL of DMEM plus 20 μL of MTS reagent to each well.
Incubate at 37 °C for 2 h.
Recover the supernatant after the MTS reaction.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean 96-well plate.
Measure absorbance of the samples at 490 nm.
Take out the incubated propeller or disk model from the incubator at days 0, 7, 15, 21, and 30.
Use a confocal spinning disk inverted microscope to visualize the spheroids.
Acquire images using multiple positions and z-stacks.
Image each propeller along its horizontal diameter from left to right with a 500 μm gap.
Acquire a z-stack from the bottom to the top focal plane at each horizontal position.
Reconstruct the image using a maximum stack arithmetic tool in ImageJ.
Create 2D images for spheroid analysis.
Prepare the alginate/gelatin hydrogel as described in step 1.2.
Put 1 mL of hydrogel into a mortar, add liquid nitrogen, and grind it using a pestle.
Continue adding liquid nitrogen to avoid the hydrogel from defrosting.
Transfer the powder into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube, seal it, and store at -80 °C for 2 h.
Freeze-dry the sample for 24 h.
Wash the hydrogel gently with DPBS twice.
Fix cells by immersion in 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min at 37 °C.
Rinse fixed cells with DPBS and freeze them with liquid nitrogen.
Freeze-dry the sample for 24 h.
Analyze the hydrogel/spheroid structure and morphology with a scanning electron microscope at 25.0 kV.
Maintain chamber pressure at 70 Pa during analysis.
Use magnification from 40X up to 5,000X for detailed observation.
